St. Catherine's Day Spiced Wine

Served at: St. Catherine's Day

Serves 6Prep 10 minCook 25 min

This warming Spiced Wine, often known as Mulled Wine, is a perfect beverage to share during the festivities of St. Catherine's Day on November 25th. Its aromatic spices and comforting warmth offer a delightful counterpoint to the crisp late autumn air, making it a cherished part of seasonal celebrations.

Ingredients

  • 1 (750 ml) bottle dry red wine (such as Merlot or Cabernet Sauvignon)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) brandy or orange liqueur (optional)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) honey or brown sugar, or to taste
  • 1 large orange, sliced into rounds
  • 1 lemon, sliced into rounds
  • 4 cinnamon sticks
  • 12 whole cloves
  • 3 star anise pods
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg (optional)

Method

  1. Combine the red wine, brandy (if using), water, honey or brown sugar, orange slices, lemon slices, cinnamon sticks, whole cloves, star anise, and ground nutmeg (if using) in a large non-reactive pot or saucepan.
  2. Heat the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally to dissolve the sweetener.
  3. Bring the wine to a gentle simmer, ensuring it does not boil, as boiling can cause the alcohol to evaporate and alter the flavor.
  4. Reduce the heat to low and let the spiced wine gently simmer for at least 20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and deepen.
  5. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired, adding more honey or sugar a teaspoon at a time until it reaches your preferred level.
  6. Strain the wine through a fine-mesh sieve into a heatproof pitcher or directly into mugs, removing all the spices and fruit. Alternatively, you can leave the fruit and spices in for presentation, removing them before serving.
  7. Serve hot in heatproof mugs or glasses, garnished with fresh orange slices or cinnamon sticks if desired.

Tips

  • Do not let the wine boil, as this will cook off the alcohol and can make the wine bitter.
  • For a non-alcoholic version, substitute red grape juice or cranberry juice for the red wine.
  • Adjust the amount of sweetener and spices to suit your personal taste preferences.
